config.documentTitleFull: PETITION TO RESTRICT AND SEAL FIRST OFFENDER RECORDS FOR A SENTENCE IMPOSED BEFORE JULY 1, 2026 THAT HAS NOT BEEN REVOKED, PURSUANT TO O.C.G.A. § 42-8-62.1(c)
config.courtCaption: IN THE [COURT THAT ORDERED YOUR FIRST OFFENDER SENTENCE — STATE, SUPERIOR, MAGISTRATE, PROBATE OR MUNICIPAL COURT; CONFIRM FROM YOUR OWN COURT RECORD] OF [COUNTY — CONFIRM FROM YOUR OWN COURT RECORD] COUNTY, STATE OF GEORGIA

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: An individual who was sentenced pursuant to Article 3 of Chapter 8 of Title 42 prior to July 1, 2026 and has not had their sentence revoked and adjudicated guilty may petition the court that ordered such sentence to limit public access to his or her case information pursuant to subsection (b). Notice of the petition shall be sent to the clerk of court and the prosecuting attorney, and notice sent by registered or certified mail or statutory overnight delivery is sufficient.

Within 90 days of the filing the court shall order restriction and sealing. The former requirement that the court find by a preponderance of the evidence that a discharge had been granted and that privacy harm outweighed the public interest was struck, so relief on a properly filed petition is mandatory and no balancing showing is required.
The clerk seals every document in its custody within 60 days of the court's order.
Law enforcement agencies, jails and detention centers must restrict within 30 days of receiving a copy of the order.

config.serviceNote: Notice of the petition shall be sent to the clerk of court and the prosecuting attorney. Notice is not a request for consent and there is no advance-consent requirement on this route; the statute creates no objection period and no objection-triggered hearing branch. Notice sent by registered or certified mail or statutory overnight delivery is sufficient; hand delivery or e-filing may also be used, certified in a certificate of service.
counselFlags: Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013. The two remedies are record restriction and sealing, and neither destroys the record. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.

A restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law.

The court level is participant data and must never default to Superior Court: a state-law offence may have been tried in a State, Superior, Magistrate, Probate or Municipal court. The caption therefore carries a confirm bracket rather than a court name.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

No statewide Georgia judiciary form exists for this relief. Local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders, so the packet instructs the participant to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing.
The prosecuting attorney receives notice of the petition. Notice is not a request for consent, there is no advance-consent gate on this route, and the packet must not describe one.

No objection-triggered statutory hearing branch is modelled, because current law does not create one. A prosecutor objection may trigger the general handoff policy, but it does not create a different statutory relief track or an opposition branch.

No privacy-harm or interests-of-justice narrative is generated or requested for this route: the preponderance findings were struck, so relief on a properly filed petition is mandatory and no balancing showing is pleaded.

The packet states that the court shall order restriction and sealing within 90 days of filing, that the clerk then seals every document in its custody within 60 days, and that law enforcement agencies, jails and detention centers must restrict within 30 days of receiving a copy of the order.
The Georgia Justice Project model petitions are a structural reference only. This is an independently drafted instrument, not a copy, and it is not represented as an official form.

Recorded non-blocking research note from the pin: the amended subsection reads on its face on anyone sentenced under the article before July 1, 2026 whose sentence was not revoked, which textually includes a person already exonerated and discharged, while a separate section provides a petition specifically for that discharged population. The adopted memorandum allocates the discharged population to the other section; this track carries the active or not-yet-discharged population.

LegalEase prompts for and formats the participant's own account of what has changed and how the record has been a barrier. It does not write the interests-of-justice or privacy-harm narrative, does not assert that the participant is eligible or likely to succeed, and does not assert that a record will be erased, destroyed, deleted or expunged.

The source requires the proposed order to name the OTN and the arrest date, name GCIC and the county agencies by category, name the clerk and court, and limit disclosure to what the statute permits; an order that does not name GCIC is not actionable. The shared custom-pleading renderer emits a fixed order body that names the custodians but cannot carry the OTN, the arrest date or the disclosure limits, and renderer changes fall outside this lane's owned paths. Recorded as a blocked component.

The shared renderer's order preamble ("AND NOW, this ______ day of ...") and its fixed section heading "VI. VERIFICATION" are Pennsylvania-derived artefacts of the frozen renderer contract, not Georgia drafting choices. Both are visual- and counsel-review items.

No statutory filing fee is identified for a motion or petition filed in an existing Georgia criminal case, and whether any clerk charges one is county-specific and unresolved. No figure is quoted anywhere in this packet and the fee field is left null.
Whether the Georgia pauper's affidavit practice reaches a filing made in a criminal case is unresolved, so no fee-waiver instrument is included and the fee-waiver field is left null.

provenance.registryExcerpt: As amended by Act 403, § 42-8-62.1(c) provides that an individual who was sentenced pursuant to Article 3 of Chapter 8 of Title 42 prior to July 1, 2026 and has not had their sentence revoked and adjudicated guilty may petition the court that ordered such sentence to limit public access to his or her case information pursuant to subsection (b). Notice of the petition shall be sent to the clerk of court and the prosecuting attorney, and notice sent by registered or certified mail or statutory overnight delivery is sufficient. Under (d), within 90 days of the filing the court shall order restriction and sealing. Act 403 struck the former requirement that the court find by a preponderance of the evidence that a discharge had been granted and that privacy harm outweighed the public interest, so relief on a properly filed petition is now mandatory and no balancing showing is required. Venue: Statewide statute. The court that ordered the First Offender sentence, in the existing criminal case. Filing: File as a criminal petition in the existing case with the clerk of the court that handled the underlying case. Confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. Fees: No statutory filing fee is identified. Because the relief is a motion or petition in an existing criminal case rather than a new civil action, the leading Georgia pro se practice does not budget one. Unresolved and county-specific; no figure is quoted. Fee waiver: Unresolved. The pauper's affidavit route under O.C.G.A. § 9-15-2 is designed for civil actions and its application to a filing in a criminal case is unresolved. Notice: Notice of the petition shall be sent to the clerk of court and the prosecuting attorney. Notice is not a request for consent and there is no advance-consent requirement on this route. The statute creates no objection period and no objection-triggered hearing branch. Service: Notice sent by registered or certified mail or statutory overnight delivery is sufficient notice under § 42-8-62.1(c). Hand delivery or e-filing may also be used, certified in a certificate of service. Participant signature: The defendant signs the petition and the certificate of service. No verification or notarization is required by statute. Notarization: none The prosecuting attorney receives notice of the petition. Notice is not a request for consent, there is no advance-consent gate on this route, and the packet must not describe one. The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No. Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders. The packet must say that the court shall order restriction and sealing within 90 days of filing, that the clerk then seals every document in its custody within 60 days, and that law enforcement agencies, jails and detention centers must restrict within 30 days of receiving a copy of the order. The participant obtains and attaches the final disposition showing the First Offender sentence as Exhibit A. Exclusion: A First Offender sentence imposed on or after July 1, 2026, which the court restricts and seals at sentencing instead. Exclusion: A case where the First Offender sentence was revoked and an adjudication of guilt entered. Exclusion: A participant who was never sentenced under the First Offender Act, who is on the separate retroactive first offender route under § 42-8-66. Exclusion: A participant who was exonerated and discharged before July 1, 2026, who is routed to the § 42-8-62.2(c) petition under the adopted crosswalk. Waiting period — Filing the petition: none — there is no waiting period Waiting period — The court's order after filing: the court shall order restriction and sealing within 90 days of the filing under § 42-8-62.1(d) Waiting period — Clerk sealing after the order: 60 days under § 42-8-62.1(e)(1) Waiting period — Law enforcement, jail and detention center compliance after receiving a copy of the order: 30 days under § 42-8-62.1(f)
